# Orch v0.1.3

**Pre-release.** The first update of the v0.1 pre-release. It fixes what the first day of v0.1.2 showed.

## Upgrade notes

- Add `ORCH_RELEASE_URL=https://github.com/mnihyc/Orchestra/releases` to `deploy/.env`, then run `./update.sh latest`. New installations have the line already.
- No database change. Connectors of v0.1.2 keep working.
- After the update, build checks run again by themselves for agent program builds that lack the new cases.

## Added

- **Build checks cover more.** A check of an agent program build now has its own cases for editing a sent message and continuing from an earlier version (Claude Code) and for ending background commands (Codex), and requires the message id used for steering.

## Changed

- A build that passed its check keeps what it proved when a later release adds cases. New cases show as pending until they have run.
- A reference written as `id:` is drawn as a chip from the start and no longer shifts the line when its name arrives.
- New installations have the release address set, so `./update.sh latest` works without a hand step.

## Fixed

- Moving another person's thread to another environment asked the mover for the right to drive the thread and to use its provider. It now asks the thread's owner whether the provider may run at the destination.
- **Move to another machine** failed while importing an environment's recorded file changes or its home.
- A place's allowed approval modes listed Auto for an agent program that cannot offer it.
- Ending a background command on a Codex build that answers in an unknown form now says so.
- A turn could run past its usage cap when the usage report that reached the cap had to be applied a second time. The cap is now looked at again until the report is in.

## Removed

- Internal working notes are no longer shipped in the repository or in the release archive.

## Known issues

- After access to a thread is given, the open thread page of the person who asked can show it as missing until reloaded.
- Lines such as "Unrecognized Codex event" can appear in a conversation.
- A build is checked only where a host that can run a check exists; elsewhere it shows **Compatibility not verified**, with its functions on.
- A thread's native history is not imported across builds of an agent program; the conversation is carried over as items.
- Claude Code older than 2.1.319 and Codex older than 0.167.0 do not start.
- Copying a thread with a very long history can exceed the API's statement time limit.

Tested with Codex 0.167.2 and 0.169.0, and Claude Code 2.1.322 and 2.1.323.
